title: X_RADIAL_LAW_NULL_PERCENTILE_APPEAL
appeal_basis: binary kill-fraction methodology replaced with null-distribution percentile scoring

P2.name: outer plateau matches CR025 and stays below cosmic

P3.name: cross-galaxy convergence
conditions: at least 3 of 4 adjacent spread decreases

P4.name: WC3 null-distribution significance
conditions: WC3 within-galaxy shuffle null over 1000 seeded trials (seeds 0..999)
each trial collects endpoint_diff = median X(0.8-1.0) - median X(0.0-0.2)

P5.name: WC4 null-distribution significance
conditions: WC4 galaxy-randomized rho null over 1000 seeded trials (seeds 0..999)
each trial collects spread_endpoint_diff = log10_spread(0.8-1.0) - log10_spread(0.0-0.2)

implementation_discipline.primary_statistic: galaxy-equal: per-galaxy bin medians first, then population median across galaxy-bin medians
implementation_discipline.log_spread_positivity: only positive galaxy-bin X values used
implementation_discipline.nonpositive_accounting: galaxy-bin level direct (not derived); per-bin alongside raw-point counts
implementation_discipline.vbar_squared_formula: V_bar^2 = V_gas * |V_gas| + Upsilon_disk * V_disk^2 + Upsilon_bul * V_bul^2

verdict_ladder.PASS: P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 all hold under canonical; WC1 and WC2 preserve P1 and P3
verdict_ladder.BOUNDARY: P1 holds under canonical but at least one of P2, P3, P4, P5, WC1, WC2 fails

rule_9_falsifier: The claim that X(r) rises monotonically with radius across the 175-galaxy SPARC population to a bound-halo plateau matching CR025, with cross-galaxy convergence at the outer edge, under canonical Lelli mass-to-light ratios, AND that this canonical signal is significantly more extreme than the null distributions generated by within-galaxy radial shuffles and galaxy-randomized normalized radius assignments.
